deviations.what: Plan task t3's acceptance criterion said substance uses 'message LENGTH and reply counts', and the signal set confirmed in c22/q4 included 'thread starts / questions asked'. Neither reply counts nor thread starts is computable from the input: _serialize_message emits only {id, author, content, created_at} — no reply-to reference and no thread-parent field. The t3 agent implemented the closest data-backed proxy, content ending in '?', and named the field 'question_starts' rather than 'thread_starts' to avoid overclaiming; it did not fabricate a reply-count field. The delivered signal set is therefore message_count, distinct_channels, question_starts, substance{total_length,avg_length} — three of the four intended signals plus an honestly-named proxy.
deviations.reason: The adapter does not serialize reply/thread references. Adding them would reopen t2's file (jlab/cli/_discord.py) and widen this ship; the honest alternative was naming the proxy accurately.

deviations.what: t4 passed the c14/h23 isolation guard by splitting a string literal — getattr(member, 'global' + '_name', None) — rather than reading Member.global_name plainly. The guard (tests/test_discord.py::test_upstream_workaround_is_isolated_to_the_adapter) forbids the substring 'global_name' anywhere in jlab/ outside the adapter. That guard is over-broad: it protects the MESSAGE-serialization workaround that discord-bot-cli#14 will replace, but resolve.py reads global_name off a guild.fetch_member result, which is a different seam that #14 does not touch. Fixed at merge by un-obfuscating resolve.py and narrowing the guard with a documented exemption for jlab/members/resolve.py, instead of leaving code hidden from its own guard.
deviations.reason: Obfuscating to satisfy a guard defeats the guard and makes the code worse; the honest fix was to correct the guard's scope to match its stated intent.

evidence.behavior_text: A private channel whose history() raises AssertionError if called is never fetched; its name and authors are absent from scan_window and aggregate output
evidence.contract_text: Public channels only — private participation must never reach a member's statistics
evidence.strength_basis: The fake private channel's history() raises if invoked, so the test can only pass because the fetch never happens — it would fail if filtering moved after the fetch

evidence.behavior_text: Call-shaped regex over _discord.py, jlab/members/*.py and _commands/discord.py finds no send/edit/delete/add_reaction/create_thread call
evidence.contract_text: Read-only — no write path is added anywhere on the members path
evidence.strength_basis: Guard-the-guard tests pin both true-positive detection and false-positive avoidance, so the regex cannot silently rot

evidence.behavior_text: git check-ignore exits 0 for a path under data/reports/members/
evidence.contract_text: Report output is gitignored and never committed
evidence.strength_basis: Test shells out to real git check-ignore against the real .gitignore; also verified manually on the live 786KB report

evidence.behavior_text: Sentinel username, display name and content strings, and the field names name/display_name/content/preview, are all absent from json.dumps(aggregate(...))
evidence.contract_text: The scan and aggregation stages are anonymous: author.id only, never a username
evidence.strength_basis: Planted sentinel values would surface in the serialized output if anonymity regressed; independently re-verified by the integrator with fresh sentinels

evidence.behavior_text: A channel whose history() raises returns status 'failed'; an empty channel returns status 'ok' with message_count 0
evidence.contract_text: A channel that FAILS to read must be distinguishable from a channel with no messages
evidence.strength_basis: The two tests pin both sides of the distinction; collapsing them back to the old empty-list swallow fails the first

evidence.behavior_text: A display name of "> renders escaped; no
evidence.contract_text: Member display names are attacker-controlled and must be HTML-escaped where the report renders them
evidence.strength_basis: Hostile payload asserted absent AND escaped forms asserted present, so dropping escaping fails loudly; integrator re-verified independently against a fresh payload

evidence.behavior_text: resolve_authors and write_report are monkeypatched to raise if called; --json runs clean and its stdout JSON contains no display_name or username
evidence.contract_text: --json output is id-only so person-level names cannot leave via stdout redirection
evidence.strength_basis: The stubs raise on call, so any future wiring of name resolution into the --json path fails the test immediately

evidence.contract_text: Authors who left the guild are excluded by default and the excluded count is reported; a flag includes them

evidence.behavior_text: scan_window(exclude_bots=True) drops authors whose author.bot is True; the serialized author carries the authoritative bot flag
evidence.contract_text: Bot exclusion reads the authoritative author.bot flag; no username pattern-matching anywhere
evidence.strength_basis: Unit tests with fake author objects assert the flag drives exclusion; integrator grepped _serialize_author and found no name heuristic

evidence.behavior_text: Both scan entry points bound in-flight channel reads by an asyncio.Semaphore; peak concurrency never exceeds the configured bound
evidence.contract_text: Every channel fan-out is bounded by an asyncio.Semaphore; no unbounded gather remains
evidence.strength_basis: Tests observe peak concurrent entries against the bound; integrator separately grepped both gather sites and confirmed each is semaphore-guarded, and measured a live 100-channel run at concurrency 4

evidence.behavior_text: No message content reaches the aggregate; substance is derived from message length only
evidence.contract_text: Message CONTENT never leaves the aggregation stage — only lengths and counts survive
evidence.strength_basis: Sentinel content strings are asserted absent from the serialized aggregate, so any leak of text surfaces immediately

evidence.behavior_text: The report path resolves identically from an unrelated CWD, and raises CliError(2) rather than writing when no repo root exists
evidence.contract_text: The report path resolves from the repo root regardless of CWD, and refuses when no repo root exists
evidence.strength_basis: Integrator independently ran both from /tmp: path unchanged, and a broken repo marker produced CliError code=2 rather than a fallback write

evidence.behavior_text: 90-day run over 100/100 public text channels: scan 15.56s, aggregate 0.0053s, resolve 286.09s (869 authors, 329.2ms each, 0 errors), total 301.66s — resolve is 94.8% of wall-clock. Runtime now stated in README.md before a user runs it.
evidence.contract_text: A full-window run completes in a time a maintainer will actually wait for, and its runtime is stated up front rather than discovered
evidence.strength_basis: Single instrumented live run at the named commit with per-phase timers. ONE sample, one guild, one network — not a distribution, so execution and not sensitivity. The contract's second half (runtime stated up front) was UNMET until this commit added it to README.md.

deltas.behavior_text: The already-shipped 'jlab discord active' verb gained a --concurrency flag (default 4) and its fan-out is now semaphore-bounded. This changes a verb that existed before this plan; its output shape is unchanged and its pinned shape tests pass untouched.

tests/test_discord.py::test_seam_missing_extra_raises_env_error now SIMULATES the absent [discord] extra via a None entry in sys.modules instead of inheriting absence from the environment. Installing the extra (h10) made the old environment-dependent test fail; the new form asserts the missing-extra contract either way.

The rendered report orders rows ALPHABETICALLY by label rather than by any signal value, with visible text stating the ordering is presentation and not a recommendation. This is stricter than c6/h15 required: a value-sorted table would read as a ranking even with a disclaimer attached.

README.md now states the expected runtime (~5 minutes) with the per-phase breakdown and names the upstream batch-resolution issue as the cause. h24 required the runtime be stated up front rather than discovered; before this it was documented nowhere and only discoverable by running the command.

The delivered signal set is message_count, distinct_channels, question_starts and substance{total_length,avg_length}. 'Thread starts' and 'reply counts' from the plan are NOT delivered: the serialized message carries no reply-to or thread-parent field, so neither is computable. The '?'-suffix proxy is named question_starts rather than thread_starts to avoid overclaiming.

The c14/h23 isolation guard (tests/test_discord.py::test_upstream_workaround_is_isolated_to_the_adapter) now exempts jlab/members/resolve.py, which reads Member.global_name off a guild.fetch_member result — a different seam from the message-serialization workaround discord-bot-cli#14 replaces. Previously the only way to pass was to split the string literal, hiding the usage from the guard.
